# Accelerator Bandwidth — Evidence, Scope & Comparability Dossier

- **Dossier:** `aec-dossier-accelerator-bandwidth-comparability-012` (release IDE-012, schema 1.0.0), as of 2026-11-11.
- **Status:** research candidate; not reviewed; scientific review pending; review owner unassigned.
- **Method:** AI-assisted source check. Interpretation standard: AEC-CS-001.
- **Evidence base:** releases `aec-ide-004-interconnect`, `aec-hbm4-evidence-release-001`; reconciliations `rc-009-mi300x-infinity-fabric`, `rc-009-rubin-memory-bandwidth`, `rc-009-nvlink6-per-gpu`; register issues `ec-mi300x-infinity-fabric-scope`, `ec-rubin-memory-bandwidth`, `ec-nvlink6-per-gpu`.

> A research candidate on metric compatibility, not an assessment of products. A comparability class says whether two published figures measure the same thing on documented terms; it never says which product is better. It records no human or scientific review and does not promote any Atlas relationship.

## 1. Research question

**What do published AI accelerator bandwidth figures establish, what do they not establish, and under which documented conditions can two of them be compared?**

- **Scope:** Memory, GPU-to-GPU fabric, host-link and scale-out bandwidth figures for AMD MI300X and NVIDIA Rubin, with the HBM4 stack and CXL/PCIe figures used by reference pathway B.
- **Time:** Sources dated 2022 to 2026-11-05; figures as recorded in releases 001 and 004 and the conflict register, with the IDE-009 reconciliations.
- **Excluded:** Measured application or collective throughput, which no reviewed source publishes; Any statement that one product is faster or better; Availability, supply and commercial terms.

**Principal findings.**

- None of the 26 figures is a measurement. Every one is an advertised, specified or calculated peak, or a figure whose peak status is not stated (14). No workload, software or method accompanies any of them.
- 12 of the 17 link and fabric figures state no direction; only one NVIDIA per-GPU NVLink figure does.
- NVIDIA's Rubin NVLink system aggregates (216 TB/s over 72 GPUs, 24 TB/s over 8) divide evenly to 3 TB/s per GPU, never to 3.6 TB/s. This is an arithmetic consistency check, not an explanation of the difference. Basis: `nm-c-nvl72-share`, `nm-c-nvl8-share`, `cp-nvlink-36-vs-3`.
- NVIDIA's eight-GPU HGX memory figure (130 TB/s) divides to 16.25 TB/s, matching neither per-GPU memory figure. Its 2 TB capacity also differs from eight times 288 GB (2,304 GB), and the page does not say whether rounding, configuration or counting explains it. Basis: `nm-b-nvl8-share`, `cp-nvl8-memory-share-vs-gpu`.
- AMD's 896 GB/s equals seven 128 GB/s links exactly, but AMD labels it a ring-of-8 aggregate and never calls it per GPU; arithmetic agreement does not settle its scope, so any comparison that relies on a per-GPU reading is indeterminate. Basis: `nm-a-7-links`, `cp-mi300x-896-vs-link-sum`, `rj-a-896-share`.
- Halving a figure to a per-direction value is permitted only where the source states the direction; for NVLink 6 that is the January 3.6 TB/s figure alone. Basis: `nm-c-36-halve`, `rj-c-3-halve`, `rj-c-3600-halve`.
- Of 14 comparisons classified, 1 comparable on documented terms, 6 conditionally comparable, 4 not comparable, 3 indeterminate.

## 2. Metric interpretation method

Every figure carries the descriptors below. A descriptor the source does not state is recorded as unknown and is never inferred.

| Descriptor | Recorded as |
| --- | --- |
| Source and locator | The registered source and the exact passage, through the release quantity, register entry or finding that already holds it |
| Product and configuration | As the publisher names them |
| Hierarchy level | memory stack, device memory, system memory aggregate, fabric link, device / superchip / system fabric aggregate, host link, scale-out port |
| Metric, units and counting convention | The publisher's wording and unit; bits and bytes kept apart |
| Direction | bidirectional or per direction only when the source says so; otherwise not stated |
| Aggregation scope | per stack, link, device, superchip or system, or unresolved |
| Topology and conditions | As stated, or unknown |
| Status | advertised, specified or calculated peak; measured; or not stated |
| Evidence class, uncertainty, restrictions | Attributed statement or bounded analysis, and what the figure may not be used for |

### Comparability classes

- **Comparable on documented terms.** Same hierarchy level, unit dimension, direction convention and status, all stated by the sources.
- **Conditionally comparable.** Comparable only after a stated rule-based normalization or with stated conditions attached to every use.
- **Not comparable.** The figures measure different things: different hierarchy level, aggregation scope or metric.
- **Indeterminate.** A descriptor needed to decide (direction, scope or counting convention) is not stated.

These classify metric compatibility. None says which product is faster or better.

### Normalization rules

- **`nr-bits-to-bytes`** — Convert a bit rate to bytes by dividing by eight. Line encoding and protocol overhead are not removed. Requires: none. Rejected when: none.
- **`nr-halve-bidirectional`** — Halve a figure to a per-direction value. Assumes the two directions are equal. Requires: direction=bidirectional; direction_basis=source_stated. Rejected when: direction=not_stated.
- **`nr-equal-share`** — Divide a stated aggregate evenly by a stated member count. Gives arithmetic consistency only, never a per-member figure the publisher states. Requires: aggregation_scope in per_system, per_superchip. Rejected when: aggregation_scope=unresolved.
- **`nr-sum-links`** — Multiply a stated per-link figure by a stated link count in the same direction convention. Requires: aggregation_scope=per_link; direction_basis=source_stated. Rejected when: direction=not_stated.

Each normalization in this dossier is recomputed by the validator, and one that breaks its rule fails the build.

## 4. Case: AMD MI300X Infinity Fabric

**Question.** What does AMD's 896 GB/s figure describe, and how does it relate to the 128 GB/s links?

Register `ec-mi300x-infinity-fabric-scope`: requires reassessment. Reconciliation `rc-009-mi300x-infinity-fabric`.

**Established by the sources.**

- AMD states the direction: 896 GB/s is a peak aggregate bidirectional figure, and each link is 128 GB/s bidirectional (IDE-009).
- AMD lists seven 128 GB/s links per GPU and calls the platform eight GPUs in a ring with full connectivity.

**Bounded analysis.**

- Seven links at 128 GB/s sum to exactly 896 GB/s; a platform-wide sum of the 28 links in a fully connected eight-GPU system would be 3,584 GB/s.
- The arithmetic is consistent with a per-GPU reading, but AMD's retrieved documents label the figure a ring-of-8 aggregate and never call it per GPU; arithmetic consistency is not a documentary statement.
- AMD's CDNA 4 paper uses the same '(8 GPUs)' label for a later figure it calls per GPU; a labelling convention in a later document does not state the scope of the MI300X figure.

**Normalizations used:**

- `nm-a-7-links` (nr-sum-links): 128 GB/s → 896 GB/s. Seven links at 128 GB/s sum to exactly 896 GB/s. Arithmetic; not a publisher statement; it is consistent with a per-GPU reading but does not establish it.
- `nm-a-28-links` (nr-sum-links): 128 GB/s → 3584 GB/s. A fully connected eight-GPU system has 28 distinct links; at 128 GB/s that totals 3,584 GB/s. Arithmetic; not a publisher statement; it shows what a platform-wide sum would be under that topology.

**Comparisons:** `cp-mi300x-896-vs-link-sum` indeterminate; `cp-mi300x-896-vs-1024` not comparable; `cp-mi300x-p2p-vs-nvlink6` indeterminate.

**Kept as recorded:** Direction is AMD-stated and is not reopened; The 2025 CDNA 4 edition with endnote MI350-007 is pending version verification and is not used as evidence.

**Open:** `u-i-amd-link-scope`: What are the per-link bandwidth, direction and encoding of MI300X's Infinity Fabric links, and is the 896 GB/s figure per GPU?

## 5. Case: NVIDIA Rubin HBM bandwidth

**Question.** What do NVIDIA's 22 TB/s and 19.2 TB/s figures for one Rubin GPU describe?

Register `ec-rubin-memory-bandwidth`: requires reassessment. Reconciliation `rc-009-rubin-memory-bandwidth`.

**Established by the sources.**

- NVIDIA gives 22 TB/s in posts dated 2026-01-05 and 2026-07-21 and on its HGX page, and 19.2 TB/s in a post dated 2026-11-05 and on its Vera Rubin NVL72 page.
- Every source gives 288 GB of HBM4 per GPU; none withdraws either bandwidth figure.

**Bounded analysis.**

- On NVIDIA's product pages the split follows the platform (HGX 22 TB/s, Vera Rubin NVL72 19.2 TB/s), and in its dated posts it follows the date (January and July 22 TB/s, November 19.2 TB/s); whether either pattern reflects different configurations is not stated.
- The HGX NVL8 row's 130 TB/s is 16.25 TB/s per GPU on even division, matching neither figure, so the row's bandwidth is not eight times either per-GPU figure. Its 2 TB of HBM4 also differs from eight times 288 GB (2,304 GB); the published figures do not explain whether rounding, a different configuration or another counting convention accounts for that.

**Normalizations used:**

- `nm-b-nvl8-share` (nr-equal-share): 130 TB/s → 16.25 TB/s. 130 TB/s over eight GPUs is 16.25 TB/s, matching neither 22 nor 19.2 TB/s. Arithmetic; not a publisher statement.

**Comparisons:** `cp-rubin-22-vs-19` conditionally comparable; `cp-nvl8-memory-share-vs-gpu` conditionally comparable; `cp-mi300x-vs-rubin-memory` conditionally comparable.

**Kept as recorded:** Neither figure is selected; No explanation (product revision, preliminary figure, operating condition) is offered without a primary source.

**Open:** `u-rubin-bandwidth`: Is Rubin's per-GPU HBM4 bandwidth 22 TB/s or 19.2 TB/s?

## 6. Case: NVLink 6 bandwidth

**Question.** What do NVIDIA's 3.6 TB/s and 3 TB/s NVLink 6 figures per Rubin GPU describe?

Register `ec-nvlink6-per-gpu`: requires reassessment. Reconciliation `rc-009-nvlink6-per-gpu`.

**Established by the sources.**

- NVIDIA gives 3.6 TB/s (January post, marked bidirectional; HGX individual-GPU row) and 3,600 GB/s (July post), and 3 TB/s (November post; NVL72 GPU column).
- Only the January post states a direction for a per-GPU figure.

**Bounded analysis.**

- Every Rubin NVLink system aggregate reviewed divides evenly to 3 TB/s per GPU: 216 TB/s over 72 GPUs, and 24 TB/s (marked bidirectional) over 8 GPUs; 6 TB/s per superchip is consistent with 3 TB/s if a superchip has two GPUs.
- No reviewed aggregate divides to 3.6 TB/s; this shows NVIDIA's aggregates are consistent with each other, not which per-GPU figure is correct or what the 0.6 TB/s difference counts.
- Fabric bandwidth is kept apart from local memory bandwidth and from any measured collective throughput, none of which is published.

**Normalizations used:**

- `nm-c-nvl72-share` (nr-equal-share): 216 TB/s → 3 TB/s. 216 TB/s over 72 GPUs is 3 TB/s, the same as the page's GPU column. Arithmetic; not a publisher statement.
- `nm-c-nvl8-share` (nr-equal-share): 24 TB/s → 3 TB/s. 24 TB/s, marked bidirectional, over eight GPUs is 3 TB/s per GPU, while the same page's individual-GPU row gives 3.6 TB/s. Arithmetic; not a publisher statement.
- `nm-c-36-halve` (nr-halve-bidirectional): 3.6 TB/s → 1.8 TB/s. 3.6 TB/s stated bidirectional is 1.8 TB/s per direction if the directions are equal. Arithmetic; not a publisher statement.

**Comparisons:** `cp-nvlink-36-vs-3` indeterminate; `cp-nvl72-share-vs-column` conditionally comparable; `cp-nvl8-share-vs-row` conditionally comparable; `cp-memory-vs-scale-up` not comparable; `cp-rack-vs-gpu` not comparable.

**Kept as recorded:** The difference is not explained by assuming a direction convention for 3 TB/s.

**Open:** `u-i-nvlink6-figure`: Is Rubin's per-GPU NVLink 6 bandwidth 3.6 TB/s bidirectional or 3.0 TB/s, and what does the 3.0 TB/s figure measure?

## 7. Conflicting disclosures and version history

- **`ec-mi300x-infinity-fabric-scope`** (requires reassessment). AMD states that 896 GB/s is a bidirectional peak aggregate and that each MI300X has seven 128 GB/s bidirectional Infinity Fabric links to its peers. The 2023 platform data sheet labels the figure a ring-of-8 aggregate. A 2025 edition of AMD's CDNA 4 paper (PID#2258402-C, 10/1/2025) is reported to state it per GPU OAM module in endnote MI350-007, but the 2026 edition omits that endnote and no copy of the 2025 edition has been retrieved and checked here, so that statement is pending version verification. None of these figures is measured application throughput. The scope stays unresolved.
  - 2026-11-09, registered: Recorded as unresolved question u-i-amd-link-scope in Evidence Release 004.
  - 2026-11-10, evidence added: MI300X data sheet and product page retrieved; both give 128 GB/s per link, the data sheet bidirectional.
  - 2026-11-10, resolved: Scope and direction resolved from AMD's data sheet: seven links at 128 GB/s bidirectional per GPU make 896 GB/s a per-GPU, both-direction aggregate. Release 004 is unchanged as a historical record; public statements are listed for revision.
  - 2026-11-11, evidence added: MI300X platform data sheet retrieved: 896 GB/s is called a bidirectional peak aggregate and labelled ring of 8; seven 128 GB/s links per GPU.
  - 2026-11-11, evidence added: CDNA 4 paper retrieved; the endnote MI350-007 cited in the PR #18 review is not in the edition published on 2026-11-11.
  - 2026-11-11, reopened: The IDE-008 resolution rested on arithmetic. AMD's documents state the direction but label 896 GB/s a ring-of-8 aggregate and never call it per-GPU, so the scope is not established. State set to requires_reassessment; public references corrected under rc-009-mi300x-infinity-fabric.
  - 2026-11-11, evidence added: Editorial review reports that the 2025 CDNA 4 edition (PID#2258402-C, 10/1/2025) states 896 GB/s per GPU OAM module in endnote MI350-007, which the 2026 edition omits. Archive retrieval was attempted and failed here; recorded as pending version verification, not as evidence and not as nonexistent.
- **`ec-rubin-memory-bandwidth`** (requires reassessment). NVIDIA publishes two per-GPU figures for Rubin memory bandwidth on current pages and in dated posts: 22 TB/s (January and July posts, HGX page) and 19.2 TB/s (November post, Vera Rubin NVL72 page). Neither is withdrawn and no NVIDIA source explains the difference, so neither is selected. Public statements present each figure with its date and source.
  - 2026-11-09, registered: Recorded as unresolved question u-rubin-bandwidth in Evidence Release 001.
  - 2026-11-10, evidence added: Vera Rubin NVL72 specification page retrieved; it lists 19.2 TB/s per GPU.
  - 2026-11-10, reassessed: State set to requires_reassessment: new evidence changes how the figures should be presented, but the conflict is not explained.
  - 2026-11-11, reassessed: HGX page registered and rechecked: it gives 22 TB/s per GPU. /hbm-memory/ already presented the split; only its reference note was corrected (rc-009-rubin-memory-bandwidth).
- **`ec-nvlink6-per-gpu`** (requires reassessment). NVIDIA publishes NVLink 6 per Rubin GPU as 3.6 TB/s (January post, HGX individual-GPU row) and as 3 TB/s (November post, Vera Rubin NVL72 page). Only the January post marks 3.6 TB/s bidirectional. No reviewed NVIDIA document explains the difference. Public comparisons cite the figure and date they use.
  - 2026-11-09, registered: Recorded as unresolved question u-i-nvlink6-figure in Evidence Release 004.
  - 2026-11-10, evidence added: Vera Rubin NVL72 specification page retrieved; it lists 3 TB/s per GPU and 216 TB/s per rack.
  - 2026-11-10, reassessed: State set to requires_reassessment; the conflict is narrowed, not explained.
  - 2026-11-11, reassessed: HGX page registered: 3.6 TB/s per GPU and 24 TB/s per eight-GPU switch. /interconnects/ updated with both product pages (rc-009-nvlink6-per-gpu); conflict stands.
- **Pending version verification:** AMD, Introducing AMD CDNA 4 Architecture (white paper), edition PID#2258402-C, footer dated 10/1/2025. Reported content is not used as evidence here until a version-identified copy is retrieved.

## 8. Permitted and prohibited comparisons

### Comparable on documented terms

- **`cp-stack-vs-stack`** — 2.05 TB/s (`fg-x-stack-jedec`) against 2.8 TB/s (`fg-x-stack-micron`). Both are per-stack peak bandwidths of a 2,048-bit HBM4 interface; they differ only in pin rate. Pathway: `cmp-stack-vs-stack`.

### Conditionally comparable

- **`cp-rubin-22-vs-19`** — 22 TB/s (`fg-b-22-gpu`) against 19.2 TB/s (`fg-b-192-blog`). The same metric for the same product from the same publisher, but the values conflict and no source explains why. Conditions: Cite each figure with its date and source; Do not select one figure or average the two; Two of the figures do not state that they are peaks. Pathway: `cmp-rubin-22-vs-19`.
- **`cp-mi300x-vs-rubin-memory`** — 5.325 TB/s (`fg-a-hbm3`) against 22 TB/s (`fg-b-22-gpu`). Both are per-accelerator peak memory bandwidth, across HBM3 and HBM4 generations. Conditions: State that both are stated peaks, not delivered throughput; State the memory generation of each; Carry the open 22 versus 19.2 TB/s conflict. Pathway: `cmp-mi300x-vs-rubin-memory`.
- **`cp-cxl-vs-pcie6`** — 256 GB/s (`fg-x-cxl`) against 256 GB/s (`fg-x-pcie6-rubin`). Both describe x16 links at the PCIe 6.0 rate, but NVIDIA does not state that its figure uses the same raw both-direction basis. Conditions: State that neither source's passage gives a direction and that the counting basis of NVIDIA's figure is not published. Pathway: `cmp-cxl-vs-pcie6`.
- **`cp-nvl72-share-vs-column`** — 216 TB/s (`fg-c-216-nvl72`) against 3 TB/s (`fg-c-3-nvl72`). The rack aggregate divided evenly over 72 GPUs equals the page's per-GPU column. Conditions: Even division is an assumption; Neither figure states a direction or whether it is a peak; The result shows the page is internally consistent, not which per-GPU figure is right. Normalizations: `nm-c-nvl72-share`.
- **`cp-nvl8-share-vs-row`** — 24 TB/s (`fg-c-24-nvl8`) against 3.6 TB/s (`fg-c-36-hgx`). On one HGX page, the eight-GPU switch figure divided evenly gives 3 TB/s per GPU while the individual-GPU row gives 3.6 TB/s. Conditions: Even division is an assumption; The individual-GPU row states no direction while the switch figure is marked bidirectional; Neither figure states whether it is a peak; The two figures may count different things; neither is corrected. Normalizations: `nm-c-nvl8-share`.
- **`cp-nvl8-memory-share-vs-gpu`** — 130 TB/s (`fg-b-130-nvl8`) against 22 TB/s (`fg-b-22-hgx`). On one HGX page, the eight-GPU memory figure divided evenly gives 16.25 TB/s per GPU against 22 TB/s in the individual-GPU row. Conditions: Even division is an assumption; Neither figure states whether it is a peak; The row's 2 TB capacity differs from eight times 288 GB for reasons the page does not give. Normalizations: `nm-b-nvl8-share`.

### Not comparable

- **`cp-memory-vs-scale-up`** — 22 TB/s (`fg-b-22-gpu`) against 3,600 GB/s (`fg-c-3600-gpu`). Local memory bandwidth and GPU-to-GPU fabric bandwidth describe different physical paths. Pathway: `cmp-memory-vs-scale-up`.
- **`cp-rack-vs-gpu`** — 130 TB/s (`fg-c-130-gb200`) against 3.6 TB/s (`fg-c-36-platform`). A prior-generation rack aggregate and a per-GPU figure differ in scope and generation. Pathway: `cmp-rack-vs-gpu`.
- **`cp-scale-up-vs-scale-out`** — 3.6 TB/s (`fg-c-36-platform`) against 1.6 Tb/s (`fg-x-scaleout`). NVLink 6 scale-up bandwidth is a device-fabric aggregate across a GPU's NVLink links to the NVLink Switch; ConnectX-9 scale-out bandwidth is a network-port rate on a different interface, path and protocol, with its own counting. Converting 1.6 Tb/s to 200 GB/s puts both numbers in one unit but does not make them the same physical metric. As arithmetic only, the advertised 3.6 TB/s (stated bidirectional) is about 18 times 200 GB/s, or about 9 times 400 GB/s if 1.6 Tb/s is per direction; neither ratio describes relative delivered throughput. Normalizations: `nm-x-scaleout-bytes`. Pathway: `cmp-scale-up-vs-scale-out`. **Divergence from the pathway, reconciled by `rc-013-scale-up-vs-scale-out`:** reference pathway B recorded `cmp-scale-up-vs-scale-out` as conditional; this dossier classifies it not comparable. The pathway treats the pair as comparable after converting bits to bytes. A unit conversion makes the magnitudes expressible together but cannot make a device-fabric aggregate and a scale-out port rate the same metric; under this dossier's rules the two sit at different hierarchy levels. The public pathway now records the corrected verdict, and the earlier one is kept in the reconciliation record.
- **`cp-mi300x-896-vs-1024`** — 896 GB/s (`fg-a-896-white-paper`) against 1024 GB/s (`fg-a-1024-white-paper`). Two different metrics in one table: P2P ring aggregate and total aggregate I/O, which AMD's text suggests adds the host-capable link.

### Indeterminate

- **`cp-mi300x-p2p-vs-nvlink6`** — 896 GB/s (`fg-a-896-platform`) against 3.6 TB/s (`fg-c-36-platform`). The scope of 896 GB/s is unresolved, and NVIDIA publishes the per-GPU NVLink 6 figure two ways. Pathway: `cmp-mi300x-p2p-vs-nvlink6`.
- **`cp-nvlink-36-vs-3`** — 3.6 TB/s (`fg-c-36-platform`) against 3.0 TB/s (`fg-c-3-blog`). The same product and nominal metric, but only 3.6 TB/s carries a stated direction, so whether the two use one counting convention is unknown.
- **`cp-mi300x-896-vs-link-sum`** — 896 GB/s (`fg-a-896-platform`) against 128 GB/s (`fg-a-7x128`). AMD's 896 GB/s equals the sum of the seven 128 GB/s links AMD lists per GPU, but whether the two quantities share a scope is the open question: AMD labels 896 GB/s a ring-of-8 aggregate and does not call it per GPU. Normalizations: `nm-a-7-links`.

### Rejected normalizations

- **`rj-c-3-halve`** — `nr-halve-bidirectional` on 3.0 TB/s (`fg-c-3-blog`): NVIDIA does not state the direction of 3.0 TB/s, so treating it as bidirectional (or as per direction) to reconcile it with 3.6 TB/s is unsupported.
- **`rj-a-896-share`** — `nr-equal-share` on 896 GB/s (`fg-a-896-platform`): The scope of 896 GB/s is unresolved, so dividing it across eight GPUs, or treating it as already per GPU, assumes the answer to the open question.
- **`rj-c-3600-halve`** — `nr-halve-bidirectional` on 3,600 GB/s (`fg-c-3600-gpu`): The July article states 3,600 GB/s without a direction; the January article's 'bidirectional' cannot be transferred to it.

## 9. Unresolved questions and missing evidence

- `u-i-amd-link-scope`: What are the per-link bandwidth, direction and encoding of MI300X's Infinity Fabric links, and is the 896 GB/s figure per GPU? Needed: AMD documentation stating Infinity Fabric per-link bandwidth, direction and encoding for MI300X.
- `u-rubin-bandwidth`: Is Rubin's per-GPU HBM4 bandwidth 22 TB/s or 19.2 TB/s? Needed: A dated NVIDIA datasheet or specification note that states per-GPU memory bandwidth and the configuration or conditions it applies to.
- `u-i-nvlink6-figure`: Is Rubin's per-GPU NVLink 6 bandwidth 3.6 TB/s bidirectional or 3.0 TB/s, and what does the 3.0 TB/s figure measure? Needed: An NVIDIA datasheet or specification stating the per-GPU NVLink 6 figure, its direction and any configuration dependence.
- `u-i-effective-bandwidth`: What collective or application bandwidth do the MI300X 8-GPU platform and Vera Rubin NVL72 achieve in practice? Needed: Measured results with disclosed workload, message sizes and method, from a vendor technical paper or independent study.
- `u-i-latency`: What latencies do these fabrics achieve, under what workloads and measurement methods? Needed: Latency measurements with disclosed methodology.
- `u-i-pcie-primary`: What do the PCI-SIG PCIe 6.0 and 7.0 specifications and announcements state about rates, encoding and payload efficiency? Needed: PCI-SIG announcements or specification summaries read directly.

## 11. Independent technical review

No review has taken place and no reviewer is assigned. Before any classification supports a public statement:

- a reviewer reads each figure's passage in its source and confirms value, unit, direction and scope;
- a reviewer checks each normalization rule and its preconditions, and each classification against them;
- the questions in the expert-review brief (`BANDWIDTH_EXPERT_REVIEW_BRIEF_012.md`) are put to specialists who volunteer, one question at a time;
- no answer is recorded as review unless the reviewer has agreed to how, and under what name, it is recorded.

## 13. Research applications

- Checking a draft comparison of accelerator bandwidth figures against the classification rules before it is published.
- Tracing any figure in this dossier to its publisher, date, exact passage and latest inspection.
- Converting rack or system aggregates to per-device values only where the rules allow, with the assumption stated.
- Listing the documents to request from a vendor before a bandwidth comparison can be defended (IDE-010 workflow B).
- Giving a specialist a single, bounded question to review against public material.
